correctness.rationale: The sample space is exactly q^(k(k+1)/2+km+m) independent coordinates for all prime powers. Conditioning on the number s of zero peripheral diagonals and eliminating nonzero peripheral diagonal entries leaves a uniform symmetric k-block plus a k-by-s rectangular block. At rectangular rank t, hyperbolic cancellation leaves s-t zero coordinates and a uniform symmetric (k-t)-block; lifting multiplicity is q^[binom(k+1,2)-binom(k-t+1,2)]. Rectangular and symmetric rank formulas give the stated all-nullity polynomial. The nonsingularity case is s=t and nondegenerate residual form. Rank-defect union bounds and the binomial CLT prove the positive-part normal corank law and sharp Gaussian transition, with no appeal to finite extrapolation. A separate checker explicitly enumerated eleven complete matrix ensembles over F2,F3,F4,F5 and fifteen small nonsingular symmetric ensembles; all tests passed. The analytic argument covers untested fields and dimensions.

value.rationale: All ranks in the canonical symmetric-matrix allowed pattern of a complete split graph constitute a motivated, complete finite-field invariant rather than an arbitrary small slice. The exact polynomial resolves all coranks, and its Bernoulli peripheral singularity mechanism gives a sharp solvability threshold at hub/periphery ratio 1/q. The critical corank has positive-part Gaussian fluctuations while exact invertibility also retains an independent finite-field nonsingular-symmetric constant; both features explain why the rank distribution differs from dense symmetric and generic sparse models. These structural boundaries are useful in random structured linear systems and are not a routine single-table substitution.
